hero.headline: Appeals court rules Trump administration transgender troop ban unconstitutional
hero.body:
A federal appeals court has ruled that the Trump administration acted unconstitutionally by expelling active transgender service members under a policy implemented by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The divided three-judge panel decision from the US Court of Appeals for Washington DC restricts the administration's ability to discharge troops currently serving in the military based on their transgender status.

The court's majority opinion found the ban to be "arbitrary, and based on animus," according to reporting on the decision. While the ruling prevents the military from removing existing transgender service members, the court allowed the armed services to continue blocking new transgender individuals from enlisting.

Hegseth responded to the decision by signaling his intention to appeal to the Supreme Court. On Monday, the defense secretary wrote on social media that he would "see you at SCOTUS," indicating his commitment to challenging the appeals court ruling.

The policy permits the Pentagon to remove transgender troops from active service. Legal experts and observers expect the government to challenge the appeals court decision, with the case likely to eventually reach the Supreme Court.

The ruling affects service members currently serving in uniform who identify as transgender. The court's decision limits the Pentagon's ability to discharge these individuals while legal proceedings continue, though the administration has made clear it will pursue further appeals to defend the policy.

This case represents part of a broader Trump administration effort targeting transgender people across multiple government sectors. The Department of Education's Office of Civil Rights announced an investigation into Smith College, one of the country's largest women's colleges, over its admittance of transgender women. The department stated the college could be violating federal law by "allowing biological males into women's intimate spaces," including dormitories, bathrooms, locker rooms, and sports teams.

The education department argued that Title IX's exemption for single-sex colleges applies only to "biological sex difference, not subjective gender identity." Kimberly Richey, assistant secretary for civil rights, stated that "an all-women's college loses all meaning if it is admitting biological males."

Smith College's admission policy allows for "any applicants who self-identify as women," including "cis, trans and nonbinary women." The college affirmed this policy in 2015 after studying the issue and consulting with students and alumni, noting that "concepts of female identity have evolved" since the college's founding in 1875.

The investigation follows a complaint filed by Defending Education, a rightwing group that targets schools over diversity policies. The administration has pursued multiple actions against transgender people, including filing lawsuits against states allowing transgender sports participation and seeking to ban access to gender-affirming medical care. Trump also banned transgender people from military service and required passports to match biological sex at birth.

cards.headline: Trump presses Israel not to strike Beirut as peace talks with Iran continue
cards.teaser: President Trump is urging Israel to avoid attacking the Lebanese capital as diplomats work on negotiations with Iran.
cards.body:
President Trump is pressing Israel to avoid striking Beirut as the US pursues peace talks with Iran. The diplomatic effort faces obstacles, with Iran's foreign minister warning that Israeli operations in Lebanon violate ceasefire agreements and threatening to suspend participation in negotiations over the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz.

A cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah is viewed as essential to advancing the broader peace process. Israel has appeared to step back from threats to attack the Lebanese capital, as the White House seeks to broker a deal under pressure from polling and Gulf allies.

cards.headline: Trump Proposes 25% Tariff on Brazilian Imports
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced a proposal to impose a 25% tariff on imports from Brazil, citing unfair trade practices as justification. The move represents the latest step in the administration's effort to expand its tariff program through Section 301 investigations, a trade mechanism that allows the US to retaliate against foreign countries for practices deemed harmful to American commerce.

Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 grants the US Trade Representative authority to investigate and respond to foreign trade barriers. The administration has increasingly relied on this tool to impose tariffs on trading partners, arguing that current trade relationships disadvantage American workers and businesses. Brazil joins a growing list of countries facing tariff threats under this framework.

Brazil is a major trading partner of the United States, with significant exports in agricultural products, steel, and manufactured goods. A 25% tariff would substantially increase costs for American companies importing Brazilian products and could prompt retaliatory measures from Brazil.

The announcement did not specify which Brazilian products would face tariffs or provide a timeline for implementation. Trade proposals under Section 301 typically undergo a period of public comment and review before taking effect. The Brazilian government has not yet issued a formal response to the tariff proposal.

This latest tariff proposal comes as the Trump administration continues reshaping its trade agenda following previous legal challenges. Earlier tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act were struck down by the Supreme Court, though the federal government has since established a refund process for importers who paid roughly 166 billion dollars in tariff fees. The refund process, which began in late April, requires importers to work with their original customs brokers to file claims through the government's Ace Secure Data Portal.

Industry observers expect the refund process to take 60 to 90 days, though businesses must factor in additional fees and potential tax implications when calculating returns. Some major shipping companies like FedEx and UPS have pledged to return tariff refunds to customers, while larger retailers including Amazon and Apple have remained silent on whether they will pass refunds along to consumers.

The new Brazil tariff plan adds to uncertainty in international trade markets at a time when businesses are already navigating supply chain disruptions and inflation concerns. Trade groups representing importers and manufacturers will likely weigh in during the comment period, particularly those dependent on Brazilian goods. The proposal underscores the administration's continued focus on using tariffs to reshape trade relationships, even as questions persist about the legal framework and long-term economic consequences of such policies.

cards.headline: Russian missile and drone strikes kill at least 13 across Ukraine
cards.body:
Russia launched a massive two-day assault on Ukrainian cities with hundreds of drones and dozens of missiles, killing at least 13 people and leaving others trapped beneath rubble. The attacks hit major urban centers including Kyiv, Dnipro, Kharkiv, Poltava and Zaporizhzhia.

The overnight strikes began at 3am Thursday with what Ukraine's air force described as 56 missiles of various types and nearly 700 drones. Ukrainian air defenses destroyed or suppressed 40 missiles and 602 drones, but many projectiles still reached their targets. The assault followed heavy daytime raids on Wednesday that killed at least 14 people and injured more than 80 others.

Kyiv bore the brunt of the attack. Five people were confirmed killed in the capital overnight, with 40 injured including two children. Kyiv's mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that a large apartment block collapsed in the city's Darnytskyi district, destroying 18 apartments. Rescue teams pulled 11 people from the rubble, though authorities said more than 10 people were still believed missing. Water and power supplies were disrupted in eastern parts of the city.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said the strikes represented "one of the longest and most massive Russian attacks against Ukraine." He stated the raids appeared designed to overwhelm air defense systems through sheer volume and intensity of weapons. Zelenskyy called for a "just response" and ordered Ukraine's armed forces to prepare retaliation options.

Wednesday's attacks included "double-tap" strikes that targeted first responders sent to initial strike sites. Strikes also hit two dozen locations associated with Ukraine's railway system and other critical infrastructure. Russian drones separately struck a UN vehicle in the southern city of Kherson.

The assault dealt a significant blow to recent claims about imminent peace negotiations. U.S. President Donald Trump had suggested a deal between Russia and Ukraine was close, citing remarks by Russian President Vladimir Putin that the war might be approaching an end. The scale and timing of these attacks appeared to undermine those assertions.

The intensity of recent Russian bombardment prompted concerns that Moscow was deliberately attempting to overwhelm Ukrainian air defenses through sustained attacks with large numbers of drones and missiles. Ukraine's intelligence assessed Russia aimed to cause "as much grief and pain as possible" during the campaign.

The strikes came as Hungary summoned Russia's ambassador in response to attacks near the Hungarian border, marking a shift in Budapest's stance following the recent election of Péter Magyar as prime minister, ending years of warmer relations between Hungary and Moscow under his predecessor.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats introduce bill to block Trump payments fund
cards.teaser: Three Democratic senators proposed legislation to prevent taxpayer money from funding payments to Trump allies who claimed government targeting.
cards.body:
Democratic Senators Mark Kelly of Arizona, Adam Schiff of California, and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan introduced legislation to prohibit the Trump administration's "anti-weaponization" fund. The bill aims to block payments through the program to the President, his family members, and associates.

The Justice Department announced it would comply with a court ruling halting the fund's establishment, though the department stated it "disagrees strongly" with the decision. Senate Republicans have called for explicit assurances that no such fund will be created.

cards.headline: South Carolina jury acquits store owner in shooting death of Black teen
cards.teaser: Rick Chow was found not guilty of murder in the death of Cyrus Carmack-Belton.
cards.body:
A South Carolina jury found store owner Rick Chow not guilty of murder in the fatal shooting of a Black teenager. The verdict came after the jury heard opening statements and evidence in the case involving the death of Cyrus Carmack-Belton.

Carmack-Belton was 14 years old at the time of his death. The trial centered on whether Chow was justified in using lethal force during the encounter at his store.

cards.headline: London Tube Strikes Proceed After Negotiations Collapse
cards.teaser: Rail union members walked off the job in a dispute over working hours, with more strikes planned.
cards.body:
Members of the RMT union proceeded with strikes on London's Tube system on Tuesday following the collapse of negotiations over working hours. The industrial action caused significant disruption to underground rail services across the capital.

Further strikes are scheduled for Thursday as the dispute continues between the union and transport authorities. The walkouts are affecting commuters and travelers who depend on the Tube for daily travel throughout London.

cards.headline: Clashes continue in Lebanon despite partial ceasefire agreement
cards.teaser: Fighting persists between Israel and Hezbollah even after both sides accepted a US-proposed cessation of hostilities.
cards.body:
Israel and Hezbollah continue clashing despite accepting a US partial ceasefire plan. The ongoing fighting threatens the fragile agreement intended to reduce hostilities along the Lebanese border.

A cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah is viewed as crucial to the broader peace process with Iran. Iran has halted talks with the U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza, complicating diplomatic efforts in the region.

cards.headline: Trump proposes 25% tariff on Brazil over trade practices
cards.teaser: The administration plans to impose steep tariffs on Brazilian goods, citing unfair trade policies.
cards.body:
The Trump administration announced plans to impose a 25% tariff on Brazilian imports, citing unfair trade practices. The proposal represents the latest effort by the administration to rebuild its tariff strategy using Section 301 investigations.

Section 301 investigations allow the US government to take action against countries it believes engage in unfair trade practices. The move targets Brazil specifically, marking a significant escalation in trade tensions between the two countries.

cards.headline: China cracks down on ghost kitchens in food delivery market
cards.teaser: Chinese regulators are targeting thousands of online-only restaurants that do not actually exist.
cards.body:
Original card text (unchanged)

China has begun a crackdown on ghost kitchens, online food vendors that operate without physical storefronts. Thousands of these virtual restaurants have emerged on food delivery apps, raising concerns among Chinese consumers.

The ghost kitchens list themselves on delivery platforms but lack actual restaurant locations. Chinese authorities are moving to regulate the practice amid growing consumer complaints about the cut-throat competition and questionable operations in the food delivery sector.

---

Note: The additional source material provided only confirms the headline and general concept from the BBC article, without offering new details beyond what's already in the original card. The second source (Tokyo litter fines) is unrelated to this story. The original card text accurately reflects the available confirmed information and should remain unchanged.

cards.headline: AI company Anthropic plans public share sale as valuation approaches $1 trillion
cards.teaser: The maker of Claude AI will offer public trading of its shares later this year.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, is preparing to offer public share trading later this year as its valuation approaches $1 trillion. The move represents a major milestone for the rapidly growing artificial intelligence sector.

The company has filed preliminary IPO paperwork, signaling its intent to become publicly traded. Anthropic's public offering could rank among the largest initial public offerings in U.S. history, alongside potential IPOs from other AI firms like OpenAI.

cards.headline: Six killed in Iowa domestic dispute, suspect found dead
cards.teaser: A domestic incident in Iowa left six people dead, with the suspected shooter dying from a self-inflicted gunshot wound.
cards.body:
Six people were killed in Iowa in what authorities are investigating as a domestic dispute. Police discovered the suspected shooter dead near a bridge, with evidence indicating a self-inflicted gunshot wound.

The incident resulted in a significant loss for the community, with authorities responding to reports at the scene.

hero.headline: Six family members killed in Iowa domestic dispute before suspect dies
hero.body:
Police in Iowa are investigating the fatal shootings of six people who authorities believe were killed by a relative who took his own life when confronted by law enforcement.

Officers responded Monday to a home in Muscatine, located about 50 miles southeast of Cedar Rapids, where they discovered four people fatally shot inside the residence, according to Muscatine police chief Anthony Kies. Two additional victims were found at other locations in what police describe as an apparent domestic-related dispute.

The suspected gunman died from a self-inflicted gunshot wound while speaking with officers at the scene. Police say the deaths involved members of a single family, making this one of the deadliest domestic incidents in Iowa in recent years.

Muscatine is a city of roughly 23,000 people situated along the Mississippi River in eastern Iowa. The community is now confronting the aftermath of a mass casualty event that has left seven people dead in total when counting the suspected shooter.

The local school district issued a response to the incident, though specific details about that response were not immediately available. Authorities have not yet released the identities of the victims or the suspect, nor have they provided information about what led to the violence.

Domestic violence incidents occasionally escalate to multiple homicides, though such extreme outcomes remain relatively rare. Law enforcement agencies across the country have increasingly focused on identifying warning signs and intervening in domestic disputes before they turn fatal. This Iowa case represents one of the more severe instances of how domestic conflict can escalate.

The investigation remains ongoing as police work to determine the full sequence of events. Authorities will likely examine the history of family relationships and whether there were any prior incidents or warning signs that might have preceded such violence.

The case highlights ongoing concerns about domestic violence prevention and intervention strategies. Experts have emphasized the importance of recognizing risk factors in abusive situations and providing resources to families experiencing conflict before situations become deadly.

Community members in Muscatine are grappling with the tragedy. The school district's response suggests school-age children may have been affected by the incident or that school officials felt it necessary to address the situation with students and families.

As the investigation continues, authorities will work to piece together the circumstances that led to the violence. The case will add to the growing body of research on domestic homicides and may inform discussions about prevention strategies and intervention methods for law enforcement responding to family disputes.

cards.headline: Russian attack on Ukraine kills at least 13
cards.teaser: Overnight missile and drone strikes hit cities across Ukraine, with rescuers searching rubble for survivors.
cards.body:
Russia launched an overnight attack on Ukraine using missiles and drones, killing at least 13 people. Rescuers are searching for people trapped beneath rubble in damaged buildings across multiple cities.

Residential buildings and civilian infrastructure were damaged in eight districts of Kyiv. The strike affected multiple population centers simultaneously, marking one of the more extensive Russian attacks in recent weeks.

cards.headline: Trump speaks with Netanyahu about Lebanon conflict threatening Iran negotiations
cards.teaser: The president expressed frustration that fighting between Israel and Hezbollah could derail ongoing talks with Tehran, sources said.
cards.body:
President Trump spoke with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu about the Lebanon conflict and its impact on Iran negotiations. Trump has been in communication with Hezbollah through intermediaries, according to Reuters. The White House is pushing for a deal amid pressure from polling and Gulf allies, though Iran is demanding concessions and has halted talks with the U.S. over Israeli operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza.

Both Israel and Hezbollah have accepted a U.S. ceasefire proposal, but fighting continues on the ground. A cessation of hostilities between the two parties is considered critical to advancing the broader peace process with Iran.

cards.headline: US military strikes on alleged drug boats have killed over 200
cards.teaser: The attacks began in September and aim to stop drug trafficking, but face questions about their legal basis and effectiveness.
cards.body:
The U.S. military has conducted strikes against alleged drug boats that have resulted in over 200 deaths since operations began in September. Military officials say the attacks are designed to disrupt the flow of narcotics.

The strikes have drawn criticism from observers who question both their legal standing and whether they effectively address drug trafficking. The operations mark a notable increase in the scale of U.S. military counter-narcotics activities.

cards.headline: South Carolina jury acquits store owner in shooting death of Black teen
cards.teaser: Rick Chow was found not guilty of murder in the death of Cyrus Carmack-Belton.
cards.body:
A South Carolina jury found store owner Rick Chow not guilty of murder in the fatal shooting of a Black teenager. The verdict came after the jury heard opening statements and evidence in the case involving the death of Cyrus Carmack-Belton.

Carmack-Belton was 14 years old at the time of his death. The trial centered on whether Chow was justified in using lethal force during the encounter at his store.

cards.headline: Body found in river search for missing 11-year-old boy
cards.teaser: Mackenzie Swift was last seen entering the River Don in South Yorkshire.
cards.body:
A body was discovered during a search for 11-year-old Mackenzie Swift, who went missing in South Yorkshire. The boy was last seen entering the River Don on Saturday evening, and rescue teams had been searching the river since his disappearance.

Formal identification of the remains has not yet been announced.

cards.headline: Bodycam footage released in murder of student Henry Nowak
cards.teaser: The victim's family says he did not die with dignity and calls knife crime a national emergency.
cards.body:
Bodycam footage has been released showing Henry Nowak being handcuffed before his death. His family has stated that he did not die with dignity and is calling for knife crime to be treated as a national emergency.

The release of the footage has renewed focus on the circumstances surrounding the student's murder and the broader issue of knife violence in the UK.

cards.headline: Anthropic Plans Share Sale as Valuation Approaches $1 Trillion
cards.teaser: The artificial intelligence company behind Claude will offer public share trading later this year.
cards.body:
Anthropic, the AI company behind Claude, is planning to sell shares to the public later this year. The move comes as the company's valuation nears $1 trillion, positioning it among the world's most valuable technology firms.

The share sale reflects growing investor appetite for artificial intelligence companies as the sector experiences rapid development and commercial expansion.

cards.headline: Steph Curry Signs Endorsement Deal with Chinese Brand
cards.teaser: The NBA star joined a Chinese company after ending his partnership with Under Armour.
cards.body:
Steph Curry signed an endorsement deal with a Chinese brand following his split from Under Armour. Chinese firms have been competing to secure partnerships with prominent athletes as they work to expand their presence as global brands.

The signing represents a shift in Curry's long-standing endorsement portfolio. Chinese sportswear and athletic companies have increased their pursuit of international sports stars to build brand recognition outside their home market and compete with established American and European brands.

cards.headline: Amazon Schedules Prime Day for Late June
cards.teaser: The retail giant will hold its annual sales event from June 23 to 26.
cards.body:
Amazon announced that Prime Day 2026 will take place from June 23 to 26, marking a four-day shopping event. The timing returns Prime Day to June for the first time since 2021, when the event was previously held during the summer months.

The extended format maintains the four-day structure Amazon adopted in recent years. The event offers deals exclusively to Prime members and has become a major sales period for the company and its third-party sellers. Amazon positioned the event as coming at a time when shoppers are dealing with inflation pressures.

cards.headline: London Tube Strikes Proceed After Negotiations Collapse
cards.teaser: Rail union members walked off the job in a dispute over working hours, with more strikes planned.
cards.body:
Members of the RMT union proceeded with strikes on London's Tube system on Tuesday following the collapse of negotiations over working hours. The industrial action caused significant disruption to underground rail services across the capital.

Further strikes are scheduled for Thursday as the dispute continues between the union and transport authorities. The walkouts are affecting commuters and travelers who depend on the Tube for daily travel throughout London.

cards.headline: Blackstone Raises $13.1 Billion for Asia Private Equity Fund
cards.teaser: The fund marks the investment firm's largest dedicated to the Asian market.
cards.body:
Blackstone has closed its largest Asia-focused private equity fund, raising $13.1 billion from investors. The fund will support buyouts and growth investments across the Asia-Pacific region.

This represents Blackstone's biggest dedicated investment vehicle for Asian markets, reflecting the firm's commitment to capturing growth opportunities in the region's economies.

cards.headline: Short Seller Andrew Left Convicted of Fraud
cards.teaser: The prominent investor was found guilty in a criminal case.
cards.body:
Andrew Left, a well-known short seller, was convicted of fraud in a criminal case. Left has been a prominent figure in financial markets through his research and trading activities focused on betting against company stocks.

The conviction follows a legal proceeding that examined Left's conduct. Short sellers profit when stock prices decline by borrowing and selling shares, then buying them back at lower prices. The case marks a significant legal outcome for a figure who has been active in identifying and publicizing companies he believed were overvalued.

hero.headline: Alphabet to raise $80 billion for AI expansion
hero.body:
Alphabet plans to raise $80 billion to fund its artificial intelligence infrastructure, the company announced. The tech giant said strong demand for its AI solutions and services from both enterprises and consumers is exceeding its current capacity.

The company stated that it is experiencing demand levels that surpass its available supply. The capital raise represents one of the largest corporate fundraising efforts in recent years and reflects the significant investment required to build and maintain AI systems at scale.

The announcement comes as competition intensifies among major technology companies to develop and deploy AI capabilities. Companies across the industry have been racing to expand their computing infrastructure to support increasingly sophisticated AI models and services. The costs associated with training and running these systems have grown substantially as models become more complex and user adoption increases.

Alphabet has been integrating AI features across its product lineup, including search, cloud computing services, and productivity tools. The company competes with Microsoft, Amazon, and other major players in providing AI services to business customers. Consumer-facing AI products have also seen rapid adoption, putting pressure on companies to scale their infrastructure quickly.

The $80 billion raise will help Alphabet build additional data centers, acquire specialized computing hardware, and expand its capacity to serve both business and individual users. The company has not specified the exact timeline for deploying the capital or detailed breakdowns of how the funds will be allocated across different infrastructure projects.

cards.headline: Nvidia introduces first AI-focused personal computers
cards.teaser: Nvidia unveiled new personal computers designed specifically for artificial intelligence agents, partnering with Microsoft, Dell, and HP.
cards.body:
Nvidia has launched its RTX Spark PC chip for Windows-based laptops and desktops, marking the company's entry into the personal computer processor market. The new superchip is designed to bring AI capabilities directly to consumer devices, positioning Nvidia to compete against Intel, Apple, Qualcomm, and AMD in the CPU market.

The chips will power new laptops from Microsoft, Dell, and HP. Nvidia says the technology could fundamentally change how people interact with computers, potentially replacing the mouse and keyboard with AI agents that handle user tasks.

cards.headline: GitHub Copilot switches to usage-based pricing
cards.teaser: GitHub introduced a new usage-based pricing system for its Copilot AI coding assistant, prompting concerns from developers about costs.
cards.body:
GitHub implemented a new pricing model for Copilot that charges users based on consumption rather than a flat monthly fee. Some users reported exhausting their entire monthly AI credit allotment within a single day of work.

The change has sparked reactions from developers who rely on the AI coding assistant for daily programming tasks. The usage-based system allocates a set amount of AI credits each month, which can be depleted more quickly for users who make frequent or complex requests to the tool.

cards.headline: Apple previews Siri overhaul for iOS 27
cards.teaser: Apple teased major changes to Siri for iOS 27, including a new dedicated app and expanded AI features ahead of its developer conference.
cards.body:
Apple released early information about iOS 27, which will feature a significant overhaul of its Siri voice assistant. The update includes a new standalone Siri app and expanded AI capabilities throughout the operating system. Apple promoted the upcoming Worldwide Developers Conference with the tagline "All Systems Glow" and released accompanying wallpapers and a playlist.

The company is building on iOS 26's Liquid Glass interface with what it describes as a more fluid design. Industry observers suggested the AI improvements might convince many users to upgrade to newer iPhone models that can support the enhanced features.

cards.headline: Nintendo Music adds CarPlay and Android Auto support
cards.teaser: Nintendo launched version 1.6.0 of its music app, adding support for car systems and a web browser player.
cards.body:
Nintendo released an update to its music streaming service that adds compatibility with Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, allowing users to listen to game soundtracks while driving. The company also launched a web browser version of the app for desktop listening.

The update includes the addition of Mario Kart World to the music library. The service provides access to soundtracks from Nintendo games, letting fans stream music from franchises like Mario, Zelda, and other popular titles across multiple platforms.

cards.headline: Water voles return to Farnham river after two decades
cards.teaser: About 300 water voles were released into a river in Farnham as part of an effort to restore the species to the area.
cards.body:
Approximately 300 water voles have been released into a river in Farnham, restoring the species to the waterway for the first time in 20 years. The reintroduction effort is part of a conservation initiative to rebuild native wildlife populations in the area.

Water voles have vanished from many British rivers over recent decades as a result of habitat destruction and predation. This release represents a key step in establishing a thriving population within the local ecosystem.

cards.headline: Rosetta probe found potential ingredients for life on comet
cards.teaser: The Rosetta spacecraft detected chemical compounds around Comet 67P that scientists believe may have helped life begin on Earth.
cards.body:
The Rosetta mission discovered a mixture of gases around Comet 67P that included hydrogen sulfide, ammonia, and hydrogen cyanide, creating an odor that would have resembled rotten eggs, ammonia, and bitter almonds. Hidden within these gases were chemical compounds that scientists believe may have played a role in the emergence of life on Earth.

The findings support theories that comets could have delivered organic molecules to early Earth through impacts. These building blocks of life may have contributed to the chemical conditions necessary for life to develop on the planet billions of years ago.

hero.headline: Hall of Fame coach Rick Adelman dies at 79
hero.body:
Rick Adelman, a Hall of Fame basketball coach who led teams to more than 1,000 wins across three decades in the NBA, has died at age 79. The longtime coach spent his career with multiple franchises including the Portland Trail Blazers, Sacramento Kings, Houston Rockets, and Minnesota Timberwolves.

Adelman compiled 1,042 wins during his NBA coaching career, ranking him among the winningest coaches in league history. He guided the Trail Blazers to two NBA Finals appearances in 1990 and 1992, and later transformed the Sacramento Kings into perennial contenders during the early 2000s. His Kings teams became known for their fast-paced, ball-movement offense that influenced modern NBA play.

The coach was inducted into the Basketball Hall of Fame in recognition of his contributions to the sport. Beyond his win total, Adelman earned respect throughout the league for his offensive schemes and player development. He coached numerous All-Star players and helped shape the careers of stars across multiple eras of professional basketball.

Adelman began his NBA journey as a player before transitioning to coaching, where he found his greatest success. He served as head coach for the Trail Blazers from 1989 to 1994, the Golden State Warriors briefly, the Kings from 1998 to 2006, the Rockets from 2007 to 2011, and the Timberwolves from 2011 to 2014. His coaching philosophy emphasized teamwork and offensive efficiency, principles that influenced a generation of coaches who followed.

Tributes from across the basketball community followed news of his death. The Sacramento Kings released an official statement honoring Adelman, and multiple NBA organizations acknowledged his impact on the sport. His legacy extends beyond statistics to his influence on how modern basketball is played and coached at the highest level.

cards.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams for Jared Verse and first-round pick
cards.teaser: The Cleveland Browns have traded star defensive end Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a blockbuster deal.
cards.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams in a blockbuster deal, sending linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to Cleveland. Garrett, 30, is a two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year and seven-time Pro Bowl selection.

Since being drafted first overall by the Browns in 2017, Garrett has established himself as one of the league's premier defensive players. He holds the most sacks (125.5), pressures (413), and tackles for loss (149) among players since his draft year. In 2025, he set the single-season sacks record with 23.

cards.headline: Eagles trade A.J. Brown to Patriots for two draft picks
cards.teaser: The Philadelphia Eagles have agreed to trade wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots for two draft picks.
cards.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles traded wide receiver A.J. Brown to the New England Patriots, receiving a first-round pick in 2028 and a fifth-round pick in 2027 in return. Brown, a three-time Pro Bowl selection, had grown frustrated during his time with Philadelphia.

The trade reunites Brown with coach Mike Vrabel in New England and ends months of speculation surrounding the star receiver's future with the Eagles.

cards.headline: NBA star Steph Curry signs shoe deal with Chinese brand Li-Ning
cards.teaser: Golden State Warriors guard Steph Curry has signed a sneaker endorsement deal with Chinese sportswear company Li-Ning.
cards.body:
Steph Curry signed a shoe deal with Chinese athletic brand Li-Ning, ending his long relationship with Under Armour. The NBA star's move to the Chinese company represents a significant win for Li-Ning in the competitive global sportswear market.

Curry had maintained a lengthy partnership with Under Armour before the surprise split that preceded this new agreement. The deal brings one of basketball's biggest stars to a Chinese brand, marking a notable shift in the athletic endorsement landscape.

cards.headline: Dallas Mavericks choose Valley View site for new arena and entertainment district
cards.teaser: The Dallas Mavericks have selected the Valley View location for their new arena, passing on a downtown Dallas City Hall site.
cards.body:
The Dallas Mavericks opted to build their new arena and entertainment complex at the old Valley View Mall site rather than a location near Dallas City Hall. The decision means the team will move away from downtown Dallas, where they currently play.

The Mavericks plan to develop an entertainment district alongside the new arena at the Valley View location. The team's choice represents a significant shift in the franchise's relationship with downtown Dallas, where professional sports venues have traditionally been located.

cards.headline: Iowa State transfer Milan Momcilovic commits to Kentucky
cards.teaser: Former Iowa State basketball player Milan Momcilovic has committed to transfer to the University of Kentucky.
cards.body:
Milan Momcilovic, a transfer from Iowa State, has committed to play basketball at Kentucky. The player was ranked as the number two transfer in the current recruiting cycle and drew interest from multiple programs including Arizona.

Momcilovic's commitment gives Kentucky a significant addition from the transfer portal. The former Iowa State star chose the Wildcats over other schools that had pursued him during the transfer process.

cards.headline: Southampton owner backs head coach Eckert despite spying campaign
cards.teaser: Southampton owner Dragan Solak said he will not dismiss head coach Tonda Eckert despite a spying scandal.
cards.body:
Southampton owner Dragan Solak has confirmed he will not dismiss head coach Tonda Eckert despite the spying scandal. Solak acknowledged to BBC Sport that authorizing a spying campaign against rival Championship clubs was a mistake.

Despite this error in judgment, Solak has pledged his continued backing for Eckert in the role. The intelligence operation targeted other teams competing in England's second tier.

hero.headline: Former 60 Minutes Executive Producer Criticizes CBS News Leadership
hero.body:
Bill Owens, the former executive producer of 60 Minutes, publicly criticized CBS News leadership and the current direction of the long-running newsmagazine program. Owens stated that CBS News and 60 Minutes are institutions where partisans and ideologues should not be employed.

His comments come as the program undergoes significant personnel changes under new leadership. The criticism reflects broader concerns about editorial independence and journalistic standards at the network.

The timing of Owens' statement coincides with the non-renewal of veteran correspondent Sharyn Alfonsi's contract. Alfonsi, who spent nearly twenty years at CBS News and more than a decade at 60 Minutes, accused the network of penalizing her for "refusing to sanitize factually accurate reporting."

Alfonsi's departure followed an editorial dispute over a segment about a prison in El Salvador. CBS News editor-in-chief Bari Weiss shelved the story, which Alfonsi said was factually accurate. Alfonsi claimed the network's silence in response to her representation's attempts to establish a path forward made her situation clear.

In a statement, Alfonsi warned that CBS management may "hide behind corporate euphemisms like 'modernization' and 'restructuring'" to explain her departure. She said the decision "sends a chilling message to the entire newsroom" and represents "a deliberate choice to penalize a journalist for refusing to sanitize factually accurate reporting."

Alfonsi criticized the network for choosing "access journalism over accountability and protecting power rather than scrutinizing it." She expressed concern that "the wall between editorial independence and corporate interest at CBS is being methodically torn down."

The upheaval extends beyond Alfonsi. Veteran correspondent Scott Pelley reportedly confronted CBS News management in a heated meeting, taking direct aim at Weiss over decisions to fire the show's executive producer, executive editor, and two correspondents including Alfonsi and Cecilia Vega.

Anderson Cooper, another veteran correspondent, also opted to leave the show. In comments tied to his departure, Cooper emphasized that "the independence of 60 Minutes has been critical." He expressed hope that "60 Minutes remains 60 Minutes" while acknowledging that programs can evolve.

The program has been a staple of American broadcast journalism for decades, known for investigative reporting and in-depth interviews. The changes to its leadership and correspondent lineup represent a significant shift for one of television's most established news programs.

CBS News has not publicly responded to the criticism from former and current staff members. The network faces the challenge of managing its restructuring while addressing concerns about maintaining the editorial standards that made 60 Minutes one of the most-watched news broadcasts in the country.

cards.headline: Jon Stewart Questions Event Organizer Connection for Trump Concert Series
cards.teaser: The Daily Show host noted that a person sharing a name with Jeffrey Epstein is recruiting talent for the Freedom 250 concerts.
cards.body:
On Monday's episode of "The Daily Show," Jon Stewart highlighted an unusual detail about Trump's Freedom 250 concert series: Jeff Epstein of Universal Attractions is recruiting performers for the event. Stewart expressed surprise at the name coincidence during his commentary.

The concert series has encountered significant setbacks, with more than half of the initially announced performers withdrawing from the events. Several artists, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride, cited concerns about the political nature of the celebration. Stewart used his platform to question which acts remain committed to performing.

cards.headline: Multiple Artists Withdraw from Freedom 250 Concert Series
cards.teaser: Vanilla Ice says he would perform for anyone, including Putin and Iran, as several artists back out of Trump-linked concerts.
cards.body:
Several artists have withdrawn from the Freedom 250 concert series linked to President Trump, including Young MC, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and country singer Martina McBride. These performers cited concerns that the event would be overly political in nature.

Vanilla Ice stated he would perform for anyone, regardless of their political affiliation. Meanwhile, Trump has publicly criticized the departing artists and considered appearing at the events himself. The concert series has faced significant cancellations, with Jon Stewart noting that more than half the scheduled acts dropped out.

cards.headline: Gotham Television Awards Recognize I Love LA and Other Programs
cards.teaser: HBO Max earned five awards at the ceremony, the most of any network, while Netflix took home fewer honors despite leading in nominations.
cards.body:
The Gotham Television Awards took place at Cipriani Wall Street in Manhattan, with I Love LA, Pluribus, and DTF St. Louis receiving top honors. Acting prizes went to Tim Robinson, Chase Infiniti, and Michael Shannon. HBO Max collected five awards, the most of any network at the ceremony.

Netflix entered the evening with 22 nominations, the highest count among all networks, but finished with fewer wins than HBO Max. The awards serve as an indicator ahead of the Emmy Awards scheduled for September, representing an early marker in the television awards season.

cards.headline: Alexa Demie Discusses Emotional Connection to Euphoria Character
cards.teaser: The actress described a moment when she realized how deeply she had connected with her character Maddy.
cards.body:
Alexa Demie opened up about her relationship with Maddy, the character she portrays on Euphoria. The actress recalled a specific moment when she understood how intertwined she had become with the role, describing Maddy as enmeshed within her.

Demie said that when she separated herself from the character, she began crying. The actress's comments reveal the emotional intensity of playing Maddy, a character she describes as unapologetic. Her remarks offer insight into the personal impact of portraying the role on the HBO series.

cards.headline: Singer Creates Viral Duet with Pre-Transition Self
cards.teaser: Musician Dylan Holloway gained widespread attention online for a video featuring past and present identities.
cards.body:
Dylan Holloway, a musician, created a duet that features both pre-transition and current versions of the artist. The video presents what Holloway describes as a conversation between past and present identities.

The recording went viral after being shared online, attracting significant attention across social media platforms. The creative approach to documenting personal transition through music has resonated with viewers and generated widespread discussion about identity and artistic expression.

cards.headline: Jamie Lee Curtis Shares Details About Sister Kelly Curtis's Death
cards.teaser: The actress paid tribute to her sister, who died at age 69, calling her a first friend and lifelong confidant.
cards.body:
Jamie Lee Curtis has announced the death of her older sister Kelly Curtis, who passed away on Saturday at age 69. In a heartfelt tribute, Jamie described Kelly as "talented" and "jaw droppingly beautiful," calling her "my first friend and lifelong confidant."

Kelly died peacefully in her home surrounded by nature. She had a career as an actor and filmmaker, appearing in films including Trading Places (1983), which she starred in alongside Jamie Lee, as well as Magic Sticks (1987) and The Devil's Daughter (1991).

hero.headline: Appeals court rules Trump administration transgender troop ban unconstitutional
hero.body:
A federal appeals court has ruled that the Trump administration acted unconstitutionally by expelling active transgender service members under a policy implemented by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth. The divided three-judge panel decision from the US Court of Appeals for Washington DC restricts the administration's ability to discharge troops currently serving in the military based on their transgender status.

The court's majority opinion found the ban to be "arbitrary, and based on animus," according to reporting on the decision. While the ruling prevents the military from removing existing transgender service members, the court allowed the armed services to continue blocking new transgender individuals from enlisting.

Hegseth responded to the decision by signaling his intention to appeal to the Supreme Court. On Monday, the defense secretary wrote on social media that he would "see you at SCOTUS," indicating his commitment to challenging the appeals court ruling.

The policy permits the Pentagon to remove transgender troops from active service. Legal experts and observers expect the government to challenge the appeals court decision, with the case likely to eventually reach the Supreme Court.

The ruling affects service members currently serving in uniform who identify as transgender. The court's decision limits the Pentagon's ability to discharge these individuals while legal proceedings continue, though the administration has made clear it will pursue further appeals to defend the policy.

This case represents part of a broader Trump administration effort targeting transgender people across multiple government sectors. The Department of Education's Office of Civil Rights announced an investigation into Smith College, one of the country's largest women's colleges, over its admittance of transgender women. The department stated the college could be violating federal law by "allowing biological males into women's intimate spaces," including dormitories, bathrooms, locker rooms, and sports teams.

The education department argued that Title IX's exemption for single-sex colleges applies only to "biological sex difference, not subjective gender identity." Kimberly Richey, assistant secretary for civil rights, stated that "an all-women's college loses all meaning if it is admitting biological males."

Smith College's admission policy allows for "any applicants who self-identify as women," including "cis, trans and nonbinary women." The college affirmed this policy in 2015 after studying the issue and consulting with students and alumni, noting that "concepts of female identity have evolved" since the college's founding in 1875.

The investigation follows a complaint filed by Defending Education, a rightwing group that targets schools over diversity policies. The administration has pursued multiple actions against transgender people, including filing lawsuits against states allowing transgender sports participation and seeking to ban access to gender-affirming medical care. Trump also banned transgender people from military service and required passports to match biological sex at birth.

cards.headline: Senate Democrats introduce bill to block Trump payments fund
cards.teaser: Three Democratic senators proposed legislation to prevent taxpayer money from funding payments to Trump allies who claimed government targeting.
cards.body:
Democratic Senators Mark Kelly of Arizona, Adam Schiff of California, and Elissa Slotkin of Michigan introduced legislation to prohibit the Trump administration's "anti-weaponization" fund. The bill aims to block payments through the program to the President, his family members, and associates.

The Justice Department announced it would comply with a court ruling halting the fund's establishment, though the department stated it "disagrees strongly" with the decision. Senate Republicans have called for explicit assurances that no such fund will be created.

cards.headline: Trump confronted Netanyahu over Lebanon military campaign in phone call
cards.teaser: The president called the Israeli prime minister during a phone call and questioned his military operations in Lebanon, according to officials.
cards.body:
President Trump confronted Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a Monday phone call over Israel's military campaign in Lebanon. According to two U.S. officials, Trump questioned Netanyahu's actions with blunt language, expressing frustration with the Israeli leader's approach to the operations.

The tense exchange underscores escalating tensions between the two leaders regarding Israel's military strategy in Lebanon. The confrontation comes as ceasefire discussions involving the U.S. continue, with Iran halting talks with the U.S. in response to Israeli operations in southern Lebanon and Gaza.

cards.headline: Maine Senate candidate Platner to meet with Senate Democrats
cards.teaser: Graham Platner will meet with Senate Democrats after reports emerged that he sent explicit messages to women following his marriage.
cards.body:
Maine Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner will meet with Senate Democrats, according to a campaign official who described the meeting as longstanding. The gathering comes after reports surfaced that Platner sent sexually explicit messages to multiple women after marrying his wife.

The meeting takes place eight days before Maine's Democratic primary, where Platner faces Governor Janet Mills in a race to challenge Republican Senator Susan Collins in November. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer had backed Mills over Platner in the contest, but Democrats now face the prospect of supporting Platner if he wins the primary despite the controversies surrounding his campaign.

cards.headline: Republican senators skeptical of Justice Department fund reversal
cards.teaser: Senator Chuck Grassley said the president must explicitly state there will be no weaponization fund after DOJ discontinued the program.
cards.body:
Republican senators expressed doubt about the Justice Department's decision to scrap its anti-weaponization fund, with Senator Chuck Grassley stating that President Trump needs to make an explicit commitment that the fund will not be revived. The Iowa senator's comments suggest skepticism among some GOP lawmakers about the permanence of the policy change.

The fund had been designed to compensate individuals who claimed they were targeted by government agencies. The Justice Department's reversal came amid growing criticism of the program from both parties, though some Republican senators indicated they want clearer assurances from the White House that similar initiatives will not be pursued.

cards.headline: Democrats face uncertainty over Maine Senate candidate before primary
cards.teaser: The party must now support Graham Platner despite media scrutiny over his relationships with women in a race considered essential to win.
cards.body:
Democrats confronted the situation Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer sought to prevent when he endorsed Governor Janet Mills over Graham Platner in Maine's Senate race. The party now faces the prospect of backing Platner, an untested candidate facing intense media examination of his relationships with women, in what they consider a must-win race against Republican Senator Susan Collins.

Maine's Democratic primary takes place in eight days. While it might be technically possible to replace candidates, such a move would be politically difficult at this stage of the race. The situation puts Democrats in a bind as they balance their need to defeat Collins with concerns about Platner's viability as their nominee.

cards.headline: California House primaries test Democratic voter sentiment on incumbents
cards.teaser: Multiple Democratic representatives in their 70s and 80s face primary challengers who have criticized their lengthy tenures in Congress.
cards.body:
House Democrats are watching California's primaries as a measure of anti-incumbency feeling among their voters. The contests mark the first time in the 2026 election cycle that multiple House Democrats in their 70s and 80s face primary opponents who have attacked them over their long service in Congress.

California Democratic Representatives Mike Thompson, Doris Matsui, and Brad Sherman, all age 70 or older, are among those facing competitive primary challenges from younger Democratic candidates. The outcomes will signal whether Democratic voters are willing to oust longtime incumbents in favor of new leadership, a question that has implications for the party's direction heading into the general election.
